newsitem.title: FRANCE: Phased Airbus integration possible - Dasa.
newsitem.headline: Phased Airbus integration possible - Dasa.

text.p: The German company in Europe's Airbus consortium said on Saturday the partnership could take on a transitional structure on the way to becoming a fully integrated corporation.
"Long term, we want an integrated company that owns its assets," Andreas Breitsprecher, a spokesman for Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (Dasa), said at the 42nd Paris air show which opened today.

Before reaching this goal, the commercial aircraft group could adopt a transitional form that has management control of members' design and manufacturing facilities, but does not own them outright, he told Reuters.
"There could be steps to achieve this," he said.

But while Dasa and British Aerospace Plc (BAe) want Airbus to become a tightly integrated entity, that has put them at odds with France's Aerospatiale which wants to hold onto its assets, particularly the aircraft design office, which it views as its crown jewel.

Aerospatiale chief Yves Michot said recently the partners had agreed to adopt a structure that would give the new Airbus a "management mandate" -- but not ownership -- over assets once the consortium becomes a joint stock company.
Breitsprecher said discussions were continuing but no agreement had been reached.

Earlier this year the Airbus partners signed a memorandum of understanding to study ways to transfer assets including design and production sites to a new Airbus, as a first step to a wider integration of European civil and defence activities.

Airbus is due to become a joint stock company in 1999. Dasa, a unit of carmaker Daimler-Benz AG, and state-owned Aerospatiale own 37.9 percent of Airbus, while BAe has 20 percent and Spain's Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (Casa) 4.2 percent.
